newsitem.title: CHILE: Massad to assess Chile tight rate policy daily.
newsitem.headline: Massad to assess Chile tight rate policy daily.

text.p: Central Bank President Carlos Massad said the bank's restrictive interest rate policy, known as "the adjustment," needs to be evaluated on a day-by-day basis.
"The adjustment needs to be looked at day by day," Massad told reporters after being sworn in as the Central Bank's new president.
But he signalled continuity in monetary policies, saying, "Central Bank policies will be maintained in every sense."
The statement gave the first sign of Massad's intentions on monetary policy as Central Bank president.
He also said the Central Bank had no plans to review its agreements with private banks to write off part of their roughly $4 billion in debt with the Central Bank.
Disagreements within the Central Bank over the debt accords led to the resignation of Massad's predecessor Roberto Zahler in June.
The bank's acting president until now, Jorge Marshall, had said recently the Central Bank would continue with restrictive credit policies until it was confident inflation was fully under control.
Massad also repeated the Central Bank's long-standing goal of bringing inflation down to "international levels" -- about four percent a year -- by the end of the decade.
-- Rodrigo Martinez/Roger Atwood, Santiago newsroom +56-2-699-5595 x211
